exercises.title: Pronunciation practice: Drinks
texts: Careful! Pay attention to how the words are stressed. The letter combination "ie" is pronounced like a long "i". In words with multiple syllables, the stress is usually on the first syllable.

exercises.title: The definite article (1)
texts: There are three definite articles in German: masculine: "der" (e.g., "der Wein"), feminine: "die" (e.g., "die Limo") and neuter: "das" (e.g., "das Bier").

A word that refers to a person, animal, place, thing, quality, idea or action is called a
"Nomen" oder "Substantiv."
Careful! In German, nouns always begin with a capital letter.

exercises.title: What would you like to drink?
texts: Sebastian möchte #p# trinken. Lisa möchte #p# trinken. Nina möchte #p# trinken.
Was möchten Sebastian, Lisa und Nina trinken?
Tip: What about you? What would you like to drink? Make up sentences like the ones in this exercise.

pages.title: A beer, please!
texts:
Germans like to drink alcohol, mostly beer and wine: with meals, at parties, in pubs or bars. People aged 16 and over are allowed to buy light alcoholic drinks like beer, wine and sparkling wine. You have to be 18 or over to buy hard liquor. If you look young, you will be asked to show identification when you order or try to buy alcohol.
If you have been drinking and your blood alcohol level is over 0.05 percent, you are not allowed to drive. There is a zero blood alcohol limit if you are under 21 because you are considered an inexperienced driver. There are also restrictions for cyclists: your blood alcohol level has to be under 0.16 percent.
It is best not to drink at all when you are driving a car or riding a bike, as you can be fined for having a blood alcohol content of 0.03 percent if you are caught driving or riding dangerously.

pages.title: Nouns: gender
texts:
The three articles
Image:
A cup of coffee, beneath it the words: der Kaffee
Image:
Deutschkurse | Nicos Weg | A1_E3_L2_Stock_9367329
Image:
A bottle of water, beneath it the words: das Wasser
German nouns have a grammatical gender. They are masculine, feminine or neuter. The article before the noun shows its gender:
masculine: der Kaffee, der Tee, der Saft
feminine: die Milch, die Limo, die Cola
neuter: das Wasser, das Bier
Unfortunately there are very few general rules as to which nouns have which articles. This means you have to learn each noun together with its article.
You will find the gender of a noun in the dictionary. It will either give the definite article or m. (= masculine), f. (= feminine), n. (= neuter).
Grammatical terms in German:
das Nomen: People and things are known as nouns. In German they are sometimes also referred to as Substantive or Hauptwörter.
der Artikel: An article is a word that can come before a noun. The words der, die and das are the three definite articles that indicate the grammatical gender of the noun.
das Genus: Every noun has a grammatical gender. The genders are masculine, feminine and neuter. Masculine nouns have the article der, feminine nouns have the article die and neuter nouns have the article das.

pages.title: Question Words: wer, was
texts:
When asking about people you use the question word wer.
Image:
An example using the question word "wer": Wer ist das? - Das ist Nico.
An example using the question word "wer": Wer wohnt hier? - Hier wohnen Katrin und Lotte.
When not asking about people, you use the question word was.
Image:
An example using the question word "was": Was trinkst du? - Ich trinke Wasser.
An example using the question word "was": Was macht Lisa? - Lisa telefoniert.

lines: In the apartment, Nico shows Nina and Sebastian the photo of his aunt
Yara. While Nina is getting drinks for everyone, they all try to work out how
Nico can find his aunt. Sebastian has already got an idea…
Wohnt sie hier in der Stadt?
Aber wo ist das? Kennt ihr Yaras Fahrradladen?
Wir haben … Apfelsaft, Wasser, Bier, Wein, Cola und Limonade.
Wir haben auch Kaffee und Tee im Angebot …
Ja, mit viel Milch, aber wenig Zucker. Ah warte, ich mach das.
Was ist mit dir, Nico? Hast du auch Durst? Was möchtest du trinken?
Alles klar. Dann nehme ich Limonade.
Also, Freunde, ich hab ’ne Idee! Wir … wir posten das Foto von Yara bei Book und
fragen: Wer kennt diesen Fahrradladen? Und so finden wir die Adresse raus.
Wo ist denn Nawin? Ist er nicht hier?
